title: Mailbox store: fair, timed connection admission shared by all connection users instead of try_lock polling on the read path
outcome: Every taker of the mailbox store connection acquires it through one fair, timed admission, so a bounded reader is not starved by blocking writers under sustained contention and reaches the typed Retryable only when the connection was genuinely unavailable for the whole bound.
acceptance: The mailbox store's connection is acquired by every user (append, acknowledge, idempotency read, dispatch-outcome wait, the read paths and reactivation) through one shared, fair, timed admission (for example a Condvar-signalled queue or a timed fair mutex), replacing the read path's try_lock polling with 1 ms sleeps and the writers' unbounded Mutex::lock.

Under sustained contention from blocking writers, a reader admitted within the bound acquires the connection in arrival order rather than losing every wake-up race; a test with concurrent writers and one reader shows the reader is not starved to the Retryable rejection while the connection was repeatedly free.
The typed Retryable rejection text, its 503 mapping and the bridge's safe-replay classification are unchanged; the full gate is green and the review pair clean.
